ai.description: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* reaches 60 mm in snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal spots and a distinctively curled, black-tipped tail. The throat features characteristic dark marbling.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* is best distinguished by its lack of visible external ear openings, a key feature absent in most other Indian agamid lizards.
ai.habitat: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* inhabits high-altitude, arid, and sparsely vegetated cold deserts of the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,000 and 5,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* exhibits a unique defensive strategy by rapidly curling and uncurling its brightly colored tail to distract predators and signal aggression.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs during its breeding season from May to July in the high-altitude regions of Ladakh, India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Phrynocephalus theobaldi* inhabits the high-altitude cold deserts of Ladakh in India, typically found at elevations ranging from 3,000 to 5,000 meters.
